pr.title: feat(copilot): teach Copilot code review the house rules, instead of paying an agent

review.body:
## Copilot review overview ### 🟡 Changes recommended Several Go instructions contradict established tooling and would cause false-positive reviews. **Review effort:** Balanced **Findings:** 3
Open (3) - [Standard-library rule incorrectly excludes approved tooling dependencies](#discussion_r4137622915) · New - [Invariant conflicts with established gnokey signing and broadcast flows](#discussion_r4137622975) · New - [Chain-function invariant mismatches existing transport and parsing design](#discussion_r4137623024) · New
What changed in this PR Adds GitHub Copilot review instructions tailored to the repository’s immutable Gno contracts and tooling conventions. **Changes:** - Defines repository-wide review priorities and CI boundaries. - Adds Gno-specific correctness guidance. - Adds Go tooling review rules. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `.github/​copilot-instructions.md` | Defines repository-wide review expectations. | | `.github/​instructions/​gno.instructions.md` | Adds Gno contract review guidance. | | `.github/​instructions/​go.instructions.md` | Adds Go tooling rules, but contains inaccurate constraints. |
--- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Learn more in the docs.

comments.body: Because this file applies to every `tools/**/*.go`, the “standard library only” rule is already false for `tools/gnocontracts`: `model.go:12` and `report_lock.go:8` intentionally import `moul.io/gnopm/pkg/gnomodlock`, which `tools/go.mod:15` requires. A review touching that integration would therefore produce a false violation. Scope this rule to contract companion commands or document the approved tooling dependency, and reconcile the authoritative `AGENTS.md` “Go companions” section at the same time.
comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,24 @@
+---
+applyTo: "tools/**/*.go"
+---
+
+# Reviewing the repository tooling
+
+`tools/` is the only Go module here. The repository root holds `vendor/gno.land`, and Go
+treats a `vendor/` in a module root as Go vendoring, so a root module would refuse to build
+and `go mod vendor` would delete the gno dependencies. **There is no Go module at the root
+and there cannot be one.** Anything placed outside `tools/` is built and tested by nothing.
+
+- **Standard library only.** No third module, no cgo. Chain reads go over plain JSON-RPC.

comments.body: This invariant contradicts the companion tools it is meant to govern: `gnohome tx -run` and `gnoblog` deliberately invoke `gnokey` to sign and broadcast with the terminal attached (`tools/gnohome/main.go:9-22`, `tools/gnoblog/diff.go:210-220`). Copilot would flag changes to these established paths. State the actual safety boundary—tools never handle key material and must preserve an explicit print/review path—and update the conflicting `AGENTS.md` section.

comments.body: The existing companion implementations do not have a single string-returning chain function: both `gnohome` and `gnoblog` use `fetchManifest` returning a map and error plus separate `qeval`, `abciQuery`, and transport functions (`tools/gnohome/chain.go:21-106`, `tools/gnoblog/chain.go:30-106`). This wording will create false findings whenever those tested boundaries change. Require network-free tests and separation of transport from parsing instead, then make the same correction in `AGENTS.md`.
comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,24 @@
+---
+applyTo: "tools/**/*.go"
+---
+
+# Reviewing the repository tooling
+
+`tools/` is the only Go module here. The repository root holds `vendor/gno.land`, and Go
+treats a `vendor/` in a module root as Go vendoring, so a root module would refuse to build
+and `go mod vendor` would delete the gno dependencies. **There is no Go module at the root
+and there cannot be one.** Anything placed outside `tools/` is built and tested by nothing.
+
+- **Standard library only.** No third module, no cgo. Chain reads go over plain JSON-RPC.
+- **Print transactions, never sign them.** A tool here holds no key and broadcasts nothing.
+- **A Makefile target is one line**, so a flag belongs on the tool and not in a recipe.
+- **`tools/auditpattern/run.go` is a byte-for-byte MIRROR** of `gnolang/gno`'s
+  `misc/audit-pattern-harness/internal/auditpattern/run.go`. **Never hand-edit it.** Re-mirror
+  and update the three constants at its top; `audit-patterns -drift <gnoroot>` re-hashes the
+  original and is what keeps the copy honest.
+- **Anything duplicated from a contract carries a comment naming the `.gno` file it mirrors**,
+  and a test pinning the two to the same behaviour.
+- **Table-driven tests, no network.** The chain-facing code is one function returning a
+  string; test the parsing, not the transport.
